newsitem.title: USA: US lawmakers propose tax break for venture capital.
newsitem.headline: US lawmakers propose tax break for venture capital.

text.p: Investors in companies capitalized at under $100 million would receive a substantial cut in their capital gains tax rate under a bill proposed on Thursday by three U.S. Representatives -- Democrat Robert Matsui and Republicans Phil English and Jim McCrery.

Matsui of California, a member of the tax-writing House Ways and Means Committee, said the bill would offer a 75 percent exclusion from tax for gains on new investments in small business stock held for at least three years. Other plans considered by Congress in the past would allow a 50 percent exclusion for investments held at least 5 years.

"The start-up cycle continues to shorten, particularly in high-tech ventures. These companies need access to capital quicker and investors are requiring more incentives to risk their money," Matsui said in a statement.
English of Pennsylvania and McCrery of Louisiana are also on the Ways and Means Committee which has jurisidiction over this tax bill. Republicans have said they want broad capital gains tax cuts.
